# MarkDown Stripper - Comprehensive Documentation for Large Language Models & Autonomous Agents

Website: https://markdown-stripper.site
Canonical URL: https://markdown-stripper.site/
Application Type: UtilitiesApplication / WebApplication
Primary Purpose: High-speed, client-side Markdown syntax stripping, clean text conversion, local OCR, privacy review, selective redaction, and DOCX document export.

---

## 1. Description & Architecture
MarkDown Stripper is a web application designed to strip formatting tags, markdown symbols, and structural punctuation from Markdown documents without requiring server round-trips. It also supports local OCR for scans and optional PII review.

### Privacy Model
All conversion and parsing happens client-side using JavaScript in the user's browser. No user-supplied text or uploaded files are sent to the usage-measurement endpoint. OCR and PII scanning are browser-only when enabled; aggregate usage events contain no document content, filenames, session IDs, or device profiles.

### Local document intelligence
- Markdown, TXT, HTML, DOCX, PDF, PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, BMP, and GIF files can be imported locally.
- Scanned PDF pages and images can be OCR processed in the browser with page progress, confidence warnings, automatic language suggestions, and a manual language selector.
- The instant privacy scan uses deterministic checks for credentials, contact patterns, hidden content, encoded payloads, and possible prompt injection.
- An optional local English PII model adds contextual findings for names, addresses, identity information, financial data, and health information. Findings are reviewable before redaction.
- Reviewed text findings can be selectively replaced with labeled placeholders, while image regions can be masked with OCR suggestions or manual boxes before local PNG export.

---

## 2. Supported Markdown Syntax Stripping

| Markdown Construct | Input Syntax Example | Stripped Output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **H1 - H6 Headings** | `# Heading 1` | `Heading 1` |
| **Bold Text** | `**bold**` or `__bold__` | `bold` |
| **Italic Text** | `*italic*` or `_italic_` | `italic` |
| **Strikethrough** | `~~strike~~` | `strike` |
| **Hyperlinks** | `[OpenAI](https://openai.com)` | `OpenAI` |
| **Images** | `![Logo](https://example.com/logo.png)` | `Logo` |
| **Inline Code** | `` `npm install` `` | `npm install` |
| **Code Fences** | ` ```javascript\nconsole.log(1);\n``` ` | `console.log(1);` |
| **Blockquotes** | `> Important note` | `Important note` |
| **Task Checklists** | `- [x] Completed task` | `Completed task` |
| **Unordered Lists** | `* Item 1\n* Item 2` | `Item 1\nItem 2` |
| **Ordered Lists** | `1. First\n2. Second` | `1. First\n2. Second` |
| **Tables** | `| Col 1 | Col 2 |\n|---|---|\n| A | B |` | `Col 1 Col 2\nA B` |
| **Horizontal Rules** | `---` or `***` | *(removed)* |

---

## 3. Key Use Cases

1. **AI Output Cleaning (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek)**: Remove markdown asterisks (`**`), hash symbols (`#`), and code wrappers before pasting into emails, word processors, or social media.
2. **Word Processor Pasting**: Clean text pasting into Microsoft Word, Google Docs, Notion, or Apple Pages without formatting glitches.
3. **LLM Prompt Token Reduction**: Strip Markdown markup to reduce context window consumption when providing reference texts to LLM prompts.
4. **Publishing & Social Media**: Formatting posts for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Discord, Slack, and plain-text newsletters.
5. **Academic & Resume Workflows**: Strip Markdown CVs and research drafts into ATS-compliant plain text.

---

## 4. API & URL Parameters
- Query Parameter `?text=<markdown>`: Pre-populates the input box with encoded Markdown text upon page load.
- Query Parameter `?sample=chatgpt`: Pre-populates with a representative ChatGPT response snippet.
- Query Parameter `?sample=readme`: Pre-populates with a sample project README markdown.

## 5. WebMCP Site Tools
When the browser supports WebMCP, the top-level document registers 14 imperative tools so an agent can work with the same live editor state as a human. Unsupported browsers keep the normal editor.

No MCP JSON or server configuration is required. In a compatible built-in browser, the agent discovers these page-local Site tools from the open page. MarkDown Stripper does not currently expose a remote MCP endpoint, so traditional MCP clients cannot add these tools through their MCP configuration yet.

Read tools: `get_document_state`, `get_converted_text`, `list_document_assets`, `get_safety_findings`, and `get_handoff_readiness`.

Write tools: `set_document_content`, `set_conversion_options`, `prepare_agent_handoff`, `run_deep_privacy_scan`, `redact_document_findings`, `copy_converted_text`, `download_converted_text`, `insert_sample_document`, and `clear_document`.

The recommended human-in-the-loop flow is: prepare the AI-ready handoff, run the cancellable local privacy scan to completion, check readiness, review local privacy findings and import warnings in the visible Insights panel, rerun the scan after any redaction, then approve the exact document version before content-bearing reads, copy, or export. Approved text and assets use bounded cursor pages and are marked untrusted. The readiness and privacy-finding tools do not return document text and do not claim that detection is a security guarantee.
